title: UK’s New Prime Minister Says He’ll Speak Up to Trump
summary: Imagine you have a friend who sometimes does things you don’t agree with. Do you stay quiet, or do you speak up? That’s the question facing the United Kingdom’s new prime minister, Andy Burnham. In his first big interview since taking the job, he talked about U.S. President Donald Trump. When asked twice if he trusts Trump, Burnham didn’t say yes. Instead, he said, “It’s a changing world, isn’t it, and you just obviously have to call things as they develop.” That means he’ll decide what to say based on what happens. Burnham made it clear he won’t be afraid to disagree. “I can’t at any point say that I won’t take a different opinion from him, that I will need to voice a different idea that is right for Britain,” he said. He even mentioned he was worried when Trump started a conflict with Iran. “I wouldn’t hold back from saying what I think is right,” he added. But being prime minister isn’t just about dealing with other countries. Burnham also talked about defense spending — how much money the country uses for its military. He wouldn’t promise to spend 3% of the country’s total income on defense by 2030, even though his own chancellor (the person in charge of money) once said that was crucial for safety. Burnham said they need to figure out the budget first. And for kids wondering if there might be a surprise election soon, Burnham said no. “I’m going to rule it out… I don’t think people want it.” He wants to focus on “getting the country back where it should be.” The opposition party, the Conservatives, said they’re ready for an election anytime.
why_it_matters: Countries, like friends, must balance being nice with standing up for what they believe is right.

background_read: The United Kingdom is a country in Europe made up of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
It has a prime minister who runs the government, while the king is the head of state.
The UK and the United States have been close allies for a long time, but sometimes their leaders do not see eye to eye on important issues.
The Conservatives are the main opposition party, which means they challenge the prime minister's plans.
Article_Structure: WHO: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and U.S. President Donald Trump
WHAT: Burnham said he will not be afraid to voice a different opinion from Trump and will speak up for what is right for Britain
WHY: Because Britain must put its own ideas first, even if that means disagreeing with a powerful ally

perspectives.description: Think it is brave to be honest with a powerful ally and shows the UK can be independent.
